title: On central P02, the aragonite boundary moved farther into lighter water than the 60 micromol/kg oxygen boundary in 2004-2022
abstract: We test whether aragonite undersaturation and low oxygen moved together on repeat P02 sections. We use joint good bottle measurements in 2004, 2013 and 2022, solve carbonate chemistry, and locate each boundary in depth and density. In nine matched bins at 28-32 N, 180-160 W, the aragonite saturation boundary moved 0.1020 kg/m3 lighter from 2004 to 2022. The 60 micromol/kg oxygen boundary moved 0.0330 lighter. Their difference was -0.0691 kg/m3 (conditional spatial 95% interval -0.0768 to -0.0627). It stayed negative at all 64 tested corners of independent cruise errors of +/-2 micromol/kg DIC, +/-3 alkalinity and +/-1% oxygen; the spatial interval envelope was -0.1285 to -0.0092. Nominal depth changes were -47.4 and -25.7 m. Oxygen at the moving aragonite boundary rose 5.1 micromol/kg, from a -16.4 fixed-density part and a +21.6 boundary-movement part. Calibration errors can reverse that net rise and the increase in depth separation. The wider section density result is not secure at all tested corners. Routine method changes retain the central result, but strict interpolation leaves too few central bins. A same-bottle measured-pH control for 2013-2022 gives a similar point estimate with an interval that includes zero. This is a chemical boundary test on sampled routes, not a basin trend, a carbon-source attribution or a measure of biological damage. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate results and full regeneration checks are included.

display.caption: Paired P02 aragonite and oxygen boundaries in 2004-2022. The central density difference remains negative at all tested calibration corners. Black intervals show conditional spatial uncertainty. Grey ranges show corner means on common support. The oxygen budget is an exact coordinate split, not causal attribution.

The central result persists under routine method changes. Strict interpolation cannot test the central result. A same-bottle measured-pH check for 2013-2022 gives a similar point estimate but is statistically unresolved.
